WITH de AS (
  SELECT r.PRSCRBR_ME, SUM(r.TRX_QTY) AS de_trx_52w
  FROM PHARMA_DEMO.RAW_3P.RXT_WKLY r
  JOIN PHARMA_DEMO.BIZ.MKT_DEF_DRIVER m
    ON m.PROD_NDC11 = r.PROD_NDC11 AND m.MKT_DEF = 'DRY_EYE'
   AND r.WK_END_DT >= m.EFF_FROM AND (m.EFF_TO IS NULL OR r.WK_END_DT <= m.EFF_TO)
  GROUP BY r.PRSCRBR_ME HAVING SUM(r.TRX_QTY) > 0
), hd AS (
  SELECT p.*, de.de_trx_52w FROM PHARMA_DEMO.CORE.PRESCRIBER p JOIN de ON de.PRSCRBR_ME = p.PRSCRBR_ME
  WHERE p.DECILE BETWEEN 8 AND 10
), lastcall AS (
  SELECT PRSCRBR_ME, MAX(CALL_DT) AS last_call_dt,
         SUM(IFF(CALL_DT >= DATEADD(day,-90,'2026-09-30'::date),1,0)) AS calls_90d
  FROM PHARMA_DEMO.CORE.CALL_ACT GROUP BY PRSCRBR_ME
)

text:
**20 of the 61 high-decile dry-eye prescribers have had no call from any team in the last 90 days** (no TEAL, CORAL or INDIGO call on or after 2026-07-02). All 20 were last called between 9 June and 1 July 2026, so the gap is roughly 3 to 3.5 months. Fourteen of them are decile 10.

| # | Prescriber (ME#) | Specialty | Decile | Territory | Dry-eye TRx (52 wk) | Last call (any team) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Jordan Stroud (ME7001005713) | Optometry | 10 | T011 (D-01) | 1,155 | 2026-07-01 |
| 2 | Sage Kendall (ME7002724136) | Optometry | 10 | T033 (D-03) | 1,142 | 2026-06-29 |

| 6 | Tatum Brandt (ME7002708298) | Ophthalmology | 10 | T044 (D-04) | 1,118 | 2026-06-28 |
| 7 | Dana Iverson (ME7003151762) | Optometry | 10 | T021 (D-02) | 1,115 | 2026-06-24 |
| 8 | Yael Brandt (ME7000071271) | Optometry | 10 | T033 (D-03) | 1,114 | 2026-06-15 |
| 9 | Casey Lowry (ME7001029470) | Ophthalmology | 10 | T053 (D-05) | 1,114 | 2026-06-19 |
| 10 | Avery Dunmore (ME7001924317) | Optometry | 10 | T011 (D-01) | 1,111 | 2026-06-21 |
| 11 | Avery Abbott (ME7000514735) | Optometry | 10 | T043 (D-04) | 1,107 | 2026-06-23 |
| 12 | Taylor Mercer (ME7002359862) | Optometry | 10 | T031 (D-03) | 1,105 | 2026-07-01 |
| 13 | Quinn Lowry (ME7002177725) | Ophthalmology | 10 | T032 (D-03) | 1,085 | 2026-06-19 |
| 14 | Kai Iverson (ME7001607557) | Ophthalmology | 10 | T023 (D-02) | 1,068 | 2026-06-16 |
| 15 | Zion Fairley (ME7000142542) | Optometry | 9 | T063 (D-06) | 1,057 | 2026-06-29 |
| 16 | Tatum Bishop (ME7000118785) | Optometry | 8 | T014 (D-01) | 922 | 2026-06-15 |
| 17 | Taylor Calder (ME7001742180) | Optometry | 8 | T013 (D-01) | 905 | 2026-06-09 |
| 18 | Avery Vance (ME7001560043) | Optometry | 8 | T054 (D-05) | 903 | 2026-06-25 |
| 19 | Wren Rourke (ME7000617682) | Optometry | 8 | T012 (D-01) | 890 | 2026-06-28 |
| 20 | Harper Iverson (ME7001314554) | Optometry | 8 | T064 (D-06) | 874 | 2026-06-26 |

**What stands out**
- **Districts:** D-01 has the most (6). D-03 has 4, D-02, D-04 and D-05 have 3 each, and D-06 has 2. Two territories have two gaps each: T011 and T044, which includes a decile-10 ophthalmologist.
- **Easy to recover:** Stroud and T. Mercer were called on 2026-07-01, one day outside the window. Taylor Calder has gone the longest without a call (since 2026-06-09).
- **Priority:** together these 20 wrote about 21,300 dry-eye TRx over 52 weeks. The 14 decile-10 optometrists and ophthalmologists should come first in TEAL (dry-eye) and CORAL call planning.

**Sources and definitions (knowledge layer)**
- **Prescriber definitions:** "high-decile" means decile 8–10 in `CORE.PRESCRIBER`. A "dry-eye prescriber" is anyone with any DRY_EYE market TRx across all 52 weeks of data, not just recent weeks.
- **Dry-eye market:** `RAW_3P.RXT_WKLY` joined to `BIZ.MKT_DEF_DRIVER` (MKT_DEF = 'DRY_EYE', within the EFF_FROM/EFF_TO dates), using the approved Prescription-to-TherapeuticMarket join path.
- **Calls:** `CORE.CALL_ACT` covers CRM calls from all teams (TEAL, CORAL, INDIGO) and all call types: detail, virtual, lunch and sample drop.
- **Territory and district:** taken from `CORE.TERRITORY`.
- **Access:** the FIELD_SALES role had access to all of these tables; no columns were masked or restricted.

**Assumptions**
- Data is as of 2026-09-30, so "last 90 days" means call dates from 2026-07-02 to 2026-09-30. The latest call in the data is 2026-09-29.
- Prescribers with no calls at all would also count, but every one of the 20 had at least one call before the window.
- Sample drops count as calls. If you only want detail calls, the list could get longer.

question: Which high-decile dry-eye prescribers have had no call from any team in the last 90 days?
answer:
**20 of the 61 high-decile dry-eye prescribers have had no call from any team in the last 90 days** (no TEAL, CORAL or INDIGO call on or after 2026-07-02). All 20 were last called between 9 June and 1 July 2026, so the gap is roughly 3 to 3.5 months. Fourteen of them are decile 10.

**What stands out**
- **Districts:** D-01 has the most (6). D-03 has 4, D-02, D-04 and D-05 have 3 each, and D-06 has 2. Two territories have two gaps each: T011 and T044, which includes a decile-10 ophthalmologist.
- **Easy to recover:** Stroud and T. Mercer were called on 2026-07-01, one day outside the window. Taylor Calder has gone the longest without a call (since 2026-06-09).
- **Priority:** together these 20 wrote about 21,300 dry-eye TRx over 52 weeks. The 14 decile-10 optometrists and ophthalmologists should come first in TEAL (dry-eye) and CORAL call planning.

**Sources and definitions (knowledge layer)**
- **Prescriber definitions:** "high-decile" means decile 8–10 in `CORE.PRESCRIBER`. A "dry-eye prescriber" is anyone with any DRY_EYE market TRx across all 52 weeks of data, not just recent weeks.
- **Dry-eye market:** `RAW_3P.RXT_WKLY` joined to `BIZ.MKT_DEF_DRIVER` (MKT_DEF = 'DRY_EYE', within the EFF_FROM/EFF_TO dates), using the approved Prescription-to-TherapeuticMarket join path.
- **Calls:** `CORE.CALL_ACT` covers CRM calls from all teams (TEAL, CORAL, INDIGO) and all call types: detail, virtual, lunch and sample drop.
- **Territory and district:** taken from `CORE.TERRITORY`.
- **Access:** the FIELD_SALES role had access to all of these tables; no columns were masked or restricted.

**Assumptions**
- Data is as of 2026-09-30, so "last 90 days" means call dates from 2026-07-02 to 2026-09-30. The latest call in the data is 2026-09-29.
- Prescribers with no calls at all would also count, but every one of the 20 had at least one call before the window.
- Sample drops count as calls. If you only want detail calls, the list could get longer.

sql.sql: SELECT MIN(CALL_DT), MAX(CALL_DT), COUNT(*) FROM PHARMA_DEMO.CORE.CALL_ACT

WITH de AS (
  SELECT r.PRSCRBR_ME, SUM(r.TRX_QTY) AS de_trx_52w
  FROM PHARMA_DEMO.RAW_3P.RXT_WKLY r
  JOIN PHARMA_DEMO.BIZ.MKT_DEF_DRIVER m
    ON m.PROD_NDC11 = r.PROD_NDC11 AND m.MKT_DEF = 'DRY_EYE'
   AND r.WK_END_DT >= m.EFF_FROM AND (m.EFF_TO IS NULL OR r.WK_END_DT <= m.EFF_TO)
  GROUP BY r.PRSCRBR_ME HAVING SUM(r.TRX_QTY) > 0
), hd AS (
  SELECT p.*, de.de_trx_52w FROM PHARMA_DEMO.CORE.PRESCRIBER p JOIN de ON de.PRSCRBR_ME = p.PRSCRBR_ME
  WHERE p.DECILE BETWEEN 8 AND 10
), lastcall AS (
  SELECT PRSCRBR_ME, MAX(CALL_DT) AS last_call_dt,
         SUM(IFF(CALL_DT >= DATEADD(day,-90,'2026-09-30'::date),1,0)) AS calls_90d
  FROM PHARMA_DEMO.CORE.CALL_ACT GROUP BY PRSCRBR_ME
)
SELECT hd.PRSCRBR_ME, hd.PRSCRBR_NM, hd.SPCLTY, hd.DECILE, hd.TERR_ID, t.TERR_NM, t.DISTRICT_ID, hd.de_trx_52w,
       lc.last_call_dt, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM hd) AS total_hd_dryeye
FROM hd LEFT JOIN lastcall lc ON lc.PRSCRBR_ME = hd.PRSCRBR_ME
LEFT JOIN PHARMA_DEMO.CORE.TERRITORY t ON t.TERR_ID = hd.TERR_ID
WHERE COALESCE(lc.calls_90d,0) = 0
ORDER BY hd.DECILE DESC, hd.de_trx_52w DESC
